eligibility_note: Bottom 40% of India's population by socioeconomic status as per SECC 2011 data; no premium required for beneficiaries.
benefit: Cashless and paperless hospitalization coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year at empanelled public and private hospitals across India for secondary and tertiary care.

eligibility_note: Available to all Indian citizens; no registration fee. Access via web browser or eSanjeevani mobile app.
benefit: Free online doctor consultation with government-empanelled doctors from home. Available in multiple regional languages. Suitable for non-emergency primary care consultations.

scheme_name: Jan Aushadhi (Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana)
eligibility_note: Open to all citizens. Medicines available at Jan Aushadhi Kendras (dedicated generic medicine stores) across India.
benefit: Quality generic medicines at 50–90% lower prices than branded equivalents. Over 1,900 medicines and 280 surgical items available.

eligibility_note: All TB patients in India, including presumptive (suspected) TB cases. Free services at all government health facilities.
benefit: Free diagnosis (including molecular testing), free complete course of treatment medications, and nutritional support (Nikshay Poshan Yojana — ₹500/month to patients on treatment).

scheme_name: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, CVD and Stroke (NPCDCS)
eligibility_note: All citizens above 30 years, with priority for rural and semi-urban populations through Sub-Health Centres and PHCs.
benefit: Free opportunistic screening for diabetes, hypertension, and common cancers at government health facilities. Referral and follow-up services for diagnosed cases.

eligibility_note: Below-Poverty-Line (BPL) families and certain unorganised-sector workers. Being progressively merged into PM-JAY in most states.
benefit: Cashless hospitalization coverage for BPL families at empanelled hospitals for most common illnesses requiring inpatient care.
